title: Water Cycle Basics
summary: This lesson explores the water cycle, describing how water moves above and below the Earth's surface. Students will examine the four main stages: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection.

sections.text: Scene: A bright, yellow sun shines down with visible heat rays on a blue expanse of liquid water, turning it into rising invisible vapor. High up in the blue sky, that same vapor cools and groups together to form fluffy white clouds. I wonder...? How does liquid water turn into vapor? Answer: Evaporation turns liquid water into vapor using heat from the sun.

Scene: Heavy clouds in the sky release falling streaks of rain and white snowflakes toward the ground below. Down on the surface, the water gathers and flows as runoff into winding rivers, deep lakes, and vast oceans. I wonder...? How does water return to the Earth? Answer: Precipitation returns water as rain or snow, and collection gathers runoff into rivers, lakes, and oceans.

key_concepts: Water cycle movement above and below the Earth surface
Evaporation using heat from the sun
Condensation forming clouds when vapor cools
Precipitation returning water as rain or snow
Collection gathering runoff into rivers, lakes and oceans
learning_objectives: Describe how the water cycle moves water above and below the Earth surface
Explain the processes of evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection
